verdict.reasoning: Patient reports symptoms for the past few days and that it is getting worse: "over the past few days I had... my skin is sore and red" and "it's, yeah, it's getting worse, like, the past few days. Way worse." Rash is itchy and widespread: "it's very itchy and, uh, dry, all over my body" and present on chest, hands, and arms.

Patient describes sore, red, very dry skin on chest, hands, and arms, especially inside elbows (antecubital fossae): "I've noticed my skin is uh, sore and red" and "it's uh, all over my chest, my hands and arms, and especially inside of the elbows... Which is the, the worst area" and "It's very itchy and, uh, dry, all over my body."

Cracks are present but no weeping or thickening (lichenification): "But, but, not the areas that are cracked" (in context of no weeping) and "So you have cracks over there" and "Is it weeping?..." "No. No." plus "Is there any thickened skin... darkened areas?" "no, no, I don't think so."

Doctor checks for systemic symptoms: "Otherwise, other than those rash, you're feeling well in yourself. There's no temperature, no joint pains, yeah? No fever?" Patient does not contradict this, implying no fever or arthralgia.
History of eczema is explicitly mentioned: "you've, got a history of eczema" and patient confirms by describing usual eczema treatments.
Patient states: "I, I have asthma" and discussion of inhaler use follows.
Patient reports using Diprobase: "usually I use a a a cream called diprobase."
Patient reports Dermol use in the shower: "in the shower I use something called dermal." (Dermol wash).

Transcript confirms over-the-counter hydrocortisone but not strength or strictly "as needed": "Over the counter Hydrocortisone... So you're using the Hydrocortisone, yeah?" No mention that it is 1% or that usage is PRN.

Doctor refers to blue inhaler and PRN use: "The blue inhaler? So you don't, you don't use it everyday, so you just use it on and off, yeah?" Patient agrees. Blue inhaler in asthma context implies salbutamol.
Doctor asks: "So do you have any allergies to any medication at all?" Patient: "No, no allergies."
Patient states: "in my family, uh, there's hypothyroidism and migraine. My mother has migraine."

Patient says: "hypothyroidism" and clarifies mother has it: "My mother." Doctor however repeats "she has hyperthyroidism." The fact claims hypothyroidism specifically, which conflicts with what the doctor documents.

Doctor characterizes condition as extensive eczema: "It looks like, you know, it is quite widespread, your eczema" and patient reports significant itch but no infection signs (no weeping, no fever, no thickened/darkened skin). This supports an extensive atopic dermatitis flare with itch but no infection signs.

Asthma appears intermittent and stable: "The blue inhaler? So you don't, you don't use it everyday, so you just use it on and off, yeah?" Patient: "Yeah. Yeah." and "But your breathing's all OK, yeah?" Patient: "OK, yeah, yeah. It's only when I have a flare."
Doctor instructs to continue emollients: "You still need to continue on your, emollients like the dermal soap, and, as well as the, diprovate. Yeah, so you still need to use those, in the interim."

Doctor plans Betnovate twice daily for a couple of weeks: "You might probably need a bit more stronger one, like betnovate or something like that... we'll try with some Betnovate first... You, you have to use it twice a day, for the next couple of weeks." Betnovate is betamethasone valerate and a thin layer is implied by "very small amount."
Doctor states: "we'll, you would probably need some antihistamines, which I'm going to prescribe... it's called the antihistamine is called Fexofenadine." This is for comfort/itch (pruritus).
Asthma medication is discussed historically, but there is no explicit advice in the plan to "continue as-needed use" of salbutamol. That continuation is implied but not stated.

Doctor confirms sending prescription to Boots: "we're going to send off the prescription to your pharmacy. It looks like Boots on the systems, is that correct?... so i'll send it across to Boot's. And it will be there for collecting."

Follow-up instructions given: "If, if there's no improvement, you need to get back to us. Or, if you have any kind of adverse reaction... you need to get in touch with us" and "If things are getting worse in the next two weeks, call us beforehand. Otherwise, wait for two weeks, take the medication and the cream."
